1: Divisions, and the foolishness of the cross

The Corinthians have split into fan clubs: "I belong to Paul", "I belong to Apollos". Paul asks, "Is Christ divided?" He preaches Christ crucified, which looks like foolishness to the world but is God's power and wisdom.
God chooses what the world thinks weak. Factions in the Church contradict the cross.
2: Paul came to Corinth without clever speeches, relying on God's power. There is a wisdom he does teach, hidden from the world's rulers and revealed by the Spirit, who knows the depths of God.
Faith rests on God's power, not on the skill of preachers. Some truths can only be received as a gift.
3: The Corinthians are still acting like infants. Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. Each builder's work will be tested by fire. "You are God's temple, and the Spirit of God dwells in you."
Ministers are servants, not celebrities. The passage about being saved "as through fire" is one the Church has read in connection with purgatory.
4: Apostles are stewards of God's mysteries, and what is asked of a steward is faithfulness. Paul contrasts the Corinthians' pride with the apostles' hunger, insults and hard work. He writes as their father in Christ.
"What do you have that you did not receive?" Everything good in us is a gift.
5: A man is living with his father's wife, and the community is proud of its tolerance. Paul tells them to remove him from the community for the sake of his salvation. A little yeast affects the whole dough.
The Church corrects serious public sin out of love, hoping for repentance. Christ our Passover has been sacrificed, so we are to live in sincerity.
6: Christians should not drag one another before pagan courts. Paul lists sins that keep people out of the kingdom, then adds: "such were some of you, but you were washed." He says to flee sexual immorality, because the body belongs to the Lord.
What we do with our bodies matters. "You were bought with a price; so glorify God in your body."
7: Paul answers questions about marriage. Husband and wife belong to each other. Marriage is good and permanent, and remaining unmarried for the Lord is a gift that allows undivided attention to him. Each should live the calling God has given.
Both marriage and consecrated celibacy are real vocations. The Church honours each.
8: Idols are nothing, so the meat is just meat. But not everyone knows that, and a believer with a weak conscience could be led into sin. Knowledge puffs up; love builds up.
Being right is not enough. Love limits its own freedom for the sake of others.
9: As an apostle Paul has a right to be supported, but he does not use it, so that the Gospel is free. He becomes all things to all people to save some. Like an athlete he trains hard for a crown that lasts.
The Christian life takes discipline. Paul himself does not take his own salvation for granted.
10: Israel was fed and led by God in the desert, yet many fell. So let anyone who thinks he stands take care. God will not let you be tempted beyond your strength. The cup and the bread are a sharing in the Blood and Body of Christ.
No temptation is irresistible, because God always gives a way out. The Eucharist makes the many into one body.
11: After instructions on conduct at worship, Paul rebukes the rich for humiliating the poor at the community meal. He hands on what he received: the words of Jesus at the Last Supper. Whoever eats and drinks unworthily answers for the Body and Blood of the Lord.
This is the earliest written account of the Eucharist. Paul's warning is why Catholics examine their conscience before Communion.
12: There are many gifts but one Spirit who gives them for the common good. As a body has many parts, so does Christ. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I do not need you."
No one in the Church is useless, and no one is the whole. If one member suffers, all suffer together.
13: Without love, tongues, prophecy, knowledge and even martyrdom are worth nothing. Love is patient and kind; it does not envy or boast. Gifts will pass away. Faith, hope and love remain, and the greatest is love.
This love is charity: willing the good of the other for God's sake. It is the measure of everything else.
14: Paul prefers prophecy, which builds up the whole assembly, to speaking in tongues that no one understands. Everything in the gathering should be intelligible and done for building up.
"God is not a God of confusion but of peace." Worship is for God and for the good of all present, not for self-display.
15: Paul repeats the creed he received: Christ died, was buried, rose on the third day, and appeared to many witnesses. If Christ is not risen, our faith is useless. But he is risen, the first fruits, and our bodies too will be raised imperishable.
Christianity stands or falls on a real event. "Death, where is your sting?"
16: Paul arranges a collection for the poor Christians of Jerusalem, to be set aside on the first day of each week. He shares travel plans and greetings.
"Let all that you do be done in love." Even money and logistics belong to the life of faith.
